original_question: What is a general classification or characterization of geodetic graphs, where a graph is geodetic when every pair of distinct vertices is connected by a unique shortest path (a unique geodesic)?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the paper’s title-level open problem: finding a general classification of geodetic graphs, which the introduction identifies with Ore’s still-unresolved question of characterizing geodetic graphs.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the central problem of the paper rather than one of its subsidiary open problems. It correctly uses the defining property of a geodetic graph—between every pair of distinct vertices there is a unique shortest path—and it asks for a general classification/characterization, which is exactly the broad unresolved theme emphasized in the title, abstract, background, and introduction.
missing_details: The paper frames this as an open problem, not as an established theorem or existing classification.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should explicitly quantify over all pairs of distinct vertices u,v in V(G).
The shortest path should be identified with the paper’s term geodesic.

The object to be determined is a general characterization/classification of all geodetic graphs, not merely examples or a classification of a special subclass such as graphs homeomorphic to the Petersen graph or Moore graphs.

If one wants the wording to sound like a true classification problem, it is helpful to say classify geodetic graphs up to isomorphism; the paper does not spell this out formally, but that is the natural stand-alone meaning of classification.
The paper treats construction, enumeration, and applications as related side problems, so the refined question should avoid drifting into those auxiliary directions.

The paper’s title-level problem does not impose extra restrictions such as fixed diameter, regularity, homeomorphism type, strong regularity, local finiteness, or simplicity; those belong only to later subsidiary problems and should not be inserted into the main question.
refined_question: Determine a general characterization/classification of geodetic graphs: classify, up to isomorphism, all graphs G such that for every pair of distinct vertices u,v in V(G), there exists exactly one geodesic in G joining u and v, where a geodesic is a shortest u-v path.
justification: The paper is a short note organized around the broad open problem named in its title and abstract, namely finding a general classification of geodetic graphs. In the background it defines a geodetic graph exactly as one in which every pair of vertices has a unique shortest path, and in the introduction it says that Ore’s question of characterizing geodetic graphs remains unresolved. The later page-8/page-9 items are explicitly presented as related open problems meant to provide insight into that main classification problem, so the closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft is the title-level characterization/classification question itself, not one of those narrower subsidiary conjectures.
